+# Six original Americas repair scopes
+
+This checkpoint preserves 89,588 distinct original requested cells across six packages, 441 native owners and 39,621 original intervals. The six package receipts and unchanged original encoded interval files are indexed by `six-original-scopes-001.json`; all fifteen pairwise spatial intersections are empty. These are original discovery scopes, with zero new qualified or accepted cells.
+
+The five-country physical input contains 389 complete original targets: Mexico158, Ecuador58, Bolivia37, Peru55 and Colombia81, covering66,919 original requested cells. Its stage preserves the original consumed and selected geometry. It is an input checkpoint; no producer execution or result is claimed here. Physical witnesses and positive support must still be established and interpreted, and country-specific source-evidence/native configurations must retain complete foreign applicability and owner joins.
+
+Panama52/22,669 cells remain in original-scope accounting but are excluded from the physical input. The exact retained source archive has conflicting rights, vintage, feature count and CRS statements. A permissive contemporaneous grant applicable to that archive has not been established; see issue2437. No source-boundary payload for Panama is published here.
+
+Source attribution and limits for the five retained inputs are recorded in `five-country-physical-001/source-stage-001/input-provenance.json`. No current legal boundary, physical land/water, accepted ownership or repair completion follows from these original scope receipts.

+Independent interpretation of the first actual stock physical389 result — 2026-10-18 UTC
+
+Reviewer: `/root/peru_original_evaluation`. **Accept as a completed source-relative diagnostic with explicit unresolved witnesses; this is not an issue-free physical cohort, source qualification or selected delivery. Qualified cells: 0. Accepted cells: 0.**
+
+I read the actual `whole-target-support.json` and execution receipt from `.cache/delivery-handoff/americas-five389-physical-001`, its consumed whole-original stage and combined source/target attribution, the original package queue/lineage, all consumed original physical metadata fragments, and the preserved comparison implementation. This is an actual-result interpretation. No physical/native/source producer, GEOS predicate or geometry repair was replayed. No repository files were edited.
+
+Scope and association
+
+The actual targets are the complete 389 intended original source members for Mexico 158, Ecuador 58, Bolivia 37, Peru 55 and Colombia 81. Their IDs match the five complete original package scopes, and combined attribution connects each result to its original source ID, canonical target and original native owner. Panama is absent. The five packages contain 66,919 original candidate cells, while the complete six-package denominator remains 89,588; neither number is a result of this physical comparison.
+
+The physical operation constructs candidates from **whole consumed original geometry**. It does not compare the canonical `selected` geometry or classify the original native candidate keys. Consequently a result’s land/water polygon is neither a repaired canonical footprint nor a count of eligible original cells. All 389 consumed/canonical geometry JSON values differ; explicit canonical topology-reconciliation flags occur for Mexico 32, Ecuador 27, Bolivia 26, Peru 24 and Colombia 41. Those prior cuts, original territorial exclusions, semantically open parent associations and complete foreign territorial competitors still require their own evidence. The 3,269 physical-source queries are GSHHG record relations, not a completed foreign-country ownership review.
+
+Actual country-level findings
+
+| Original package | Whole targets | Actual query relations | Targets retaining issues | Targets with nonempty mapped-water support | Targets with nonempty outside-L1 context |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Mexico | 158 | 2,193 | 60 | 27 | 109 |
+| Ecuador | 58 | 314 | 15 | 3 | 29 |
+| Bolivia | 37 | 66 | 16 | 16 | 0 |
+| Peru | 55 | 261 | 12 | 8 | 31 |
+| Colombia | 81 | 435 | 18 | 5 | 43 |
+
+Every target has some mapped-land support. That establishes neither full land coverage nor approval: 212 whole source targets also have nonempty `outside_mapped_L1_context`. This field is the part outside mapped level 1 source context, not a new legal sea boundary or present-day ocean finding. Bolivia’s zero exterior count follows this run’s source-relative relations and does not settle its water support or territorial limits.
+
+There are 121 targets with at least one retained issue and 268 without a listed issue. Across the complete result the issue geometries are: 78 `extra_reconstruction`, 54 `missing_reconstruction`, 59 `contradictory_land_water_support`, 22 `L2-outside-L1` and 2 `L3-outside-L2`. These overlap across targets and cannot be summed into unique owners or cells. No invalid-source, unsupported-level, unknown query, failed container-chain or geometry-operation-failed issue is recorded in this actual cohort. Exit0 means the diagnostic completed and retained its findings; it does not erase them.
+
+Query completeness and real witness meanings
+
+Independently of the result’s stored query lists, I read all 188,612 original physical metadata records and derived conservative numeric bounding-box expectations from each actual consumed whole target in the three explicit periodic frames. All 3,269 expected record/frame pairs are present, with no missing or extra pair in any country. The level context includes mainland/coastal/island level 1 records, level 2 water records and level 3 records where applicable. This establishes completeness against the retained metadata envelopes used by this operation. It is not a proof that GSHHG inventories every real island/water body, that its observations are contemporary, or an independent rerun of exact intersection predicates. Details are in `metadata-query-context.json`.
+
+All 3,269 actual relations report `checked`, with four substantive witness branches: 1,354 explicit disjoint predicates; 1,032 complete-source-record reconstructions where the candidate covers the source; 177 complete-candidate reconstructions where the source covers the candidate; and 706 complete operation pointsets for non-covering intersections. The last group retains 492 Polygon and 214 MultiPolygon intersection witnesses. The producer’s actual preserved method distinguishes these cases by full-geometry predicates, rather than treating an empty query list or a bounding-box hit as physical support. The disjoint records are retained tested negatives; the covering branches use complete operands rather than invented clipped witnesses.
+
+This review did not independently rerun those exact predicates. Its substantive confidence is limited to reading the genuine executed producer and the actual complete inputs/results, the independently derived conservative-query scope, and the retained relation/witness records. Source-specific observation dates, original registration/accuracy, physical authority and modern applicability remain the inherited source limitations.
+
+Computed reconstruction/overlap witnesses must remain unresolved
+
+The preserved method alternates support through level 1 land minus level 2 water, adds level 3 land minus level 4 water, and reports hierarchy disagreement separately. It also compares the resulting support/exterior footprint to the whole candidate. The actual issue entries carry the same geometries as their corresponding final support fields. These are real diagnostic witnesses, not merely repeated counters.
+
+In particular, **all 59 targets with nonempty mapped-water support also have a nonempty computed land/water-overlap witness**. The physical result therefore cannot honestly be summarized as fully consistent alternating support. Some reconstruction/overlap witnesses have thin polygonal coordinate sequences, but visual appearance is not an approved tolerance, area result or disposition. I did not calculate an area, discount a witness, introduce snapping/buffering, or label the overlap a contemporary physical contradiction. In exact set arithmetic these reconstruction and mutually exclusive support identities should hold under consistent inputs and nesting; this run records computational/source-relative discrepancies that require an explicit supported interpretation before affirmative qualification of affected records.
+
+Whole original water context is preserved: Mexico’s 6 original water-class cells belong to 2 intended owners, Ecuador’s 3 to 1, Bolivia’s 1,337 to 12, and Peru’s 2,208 to 8; Colombia has no original water-class candidate cells. Every such original water owner has nonempty whole-target water support in the actual result. Conversely, whole-target water support also appears outside original water-owner cohorts, notably five Colombia targets, because this operation evaluates whole polygons rather than only original candidate intervals. It would be incorrect to transfer the counts of water-support targets or issue targets directly into native candidate-cell decisions.
+
+The Bolivia/Peru source context especially requires preserving cross-target witnesses. Source record 180526 appears in both countries’ queried targets; the result retains the relevant nested level 3 context and hierarchy disagreements rather than assigning it by country name. Bolivia Los Andes retains `L3-outside-L2`; Manco Kapac and multiple Peru owners retain reconstruction and/or computed overlap witnesses. Neither an administrative name nor a source-country label resolves these physical hierarchy findings. The prior Bolivia 26/11 explicit-topology distinction also remains applicable; an unflagged record does not establish an unchanged footprint or permission to fill a difference.
+
+What this run advances and what remains
+
+The first whole-original physical operation is now actual evidence, covering the intended five-country 389 scope with a conservative complete metadata-query inventory and real retained relation/reconstruction witnesses. It advances the prior unexecuted physical comparison obligation. Its result does not qualify original-source rights/authority/vintage, approve a canonical territorial exclusion, establish complete foreign applicability, prove current native owner zero, or demonstrate zero-reassignment conservation. The 268 targets without listed issues acquire no automatic qualified credit; the 121 issue targets must keep their exact witnesses and supported disposition through the existing downstream route. A native diagnostic may preserve those issues without converting a whole-target flag into a fabricated cell count.
+
+Keep Panama’s 52 owners and 22,669 original cells in the six-scope denominator, with the exact historical internal rights conflict still blocked and no Panama source geometry included in this run. The result grants no permission or source-policy exception for Panama or any of the five admitted source families. All five retain their original country-specific source reviews and semantically open framework limits.
+
+Observed execution is also bounded honestly: the outer invocation exited 0 in 37.745 seconds; the result reports 36.6767 seconds internally. `/usr/bin/time -l` reported 555,057,152 bytes peak memory. These are genuine observations, not an enforced RSS ceiling, hard deadline, process-tree peak or a claim of prospective resource containment. No retrospective admission is inferred from successful completion.
+
+Separate reviewer outputs are `actual-result-interpretation.json`, `target-water-issue-context.json`, `metadata-query-context.json` and this review. They preserve whole-target interpretation and precise limits, not a new qualification framework or schema checklist. The retained comparison source was read, not executed. Standing ordinary Git authorization forwarded by Main remains in effect subject to mandatory permission/safety requirements; this review made only read-only Git accesses and no public posts, and expands no separately approved posting scope.

I found no mismatch in the original-to-supported/held partition, actual constructor ledgers, owner identities, declared land/water classes, retained source operands, or actual execution custody examined here. This is a review of completed qualification products. **Accepted cells remain zero in this review, and current owner-zero has not been established.**

Across the original scopes there are 63,365 land cells and 3,554 inland-water cells; qualification has not relabeled inland water as land. The 23 wholly held targets remain present in the retained original evidence and diagnostic custody. Narrowing the constructor's requested roster to 366 surviving targets has not removed their original records.
+
+## What was actually reconciled

+The task-side verifier `review-qualification.mjs` authenticated the pinned input blobs by commit, exact tree path/mode/OID, Git object bytes and SHA-256, then joined the original intervals, source roster, complete original requested patch, original diagnostic decisions, supported input partition, held originals and actual emitted constructor rows. `review.stdout` contains the complete resulting custody pins and country outcomes; `review.stderr` is empty. The initial harness assertion about a version/config field was corrected and its first-attempt logs remain retained separately; it was not an input or constructor failure.
+
+Supported inputs are pinned at `db3801d77516795a6f9b09a241f1196cdc1ccd49`, under `coordination/engineering/americas-original-repair-20261017/country-supported-inputs-001/{mex,ecu,bol,per,col}/`. The original evidence and requested patches remain pinned at `b6900b2fe487f3971045b63fb51c39dd30e013f3`, under `country-source-evidence-001/`. The unchanged full diagnostic decisions are at `049a96969256c7a954b0d0d8b0b6f3a6a85ced87`, under `country-diagnostics-001/`. The roots share the preceding `coordination/engineering/americas-original-repair-20261017/` prefix. Each output preparation's complete file inventory and hashes match the emitted files. Actual `authority-binding.json` and `original-rule-preimage.json` bind the supported input descriptors; the canonical rule hash and component IDs match the real constructor. I used the unchanged accepted `verifyCompletedSourceTargetNativeAuthority` for completed-result joins and independently compared every interval key and class. This did not replay physical construction, native predicates, or source geometry scans.

Its base geometry equals the retained original stage's selected geometry, its geometry hash matches the canonical value, and the physical receipt remains the original receipt. Whole original and selected geometries differ for all 389 targets. Qualification does not erase any of these findings or certify a whole parent. The unchanged accepted constructor evaluates requested native centres against the retained residual/conflict witnesses, source coverage, declared class support and territorial exclusions. Its actual completed products apply to the requested keys only. The retained original diagnostic found territorial exclusion to be the reason for all 3,884 held keys; none were reassigned to an adjacent owner.
+

They retain 5 / 4 / 11 / 11 / 10 foreign families for MEX / ECU / BOL / PER / COL respectively, and surviving targets retain 131 / 111 / 150 / 182 / 123 explicit negative constraints (697 total). Brazil is an existing foreign operand where applicable, not a hardcoded positive selection. Colombia retains both Panama ADM1 and ADM2 negative families. The prior review establishes completeness within the recorded bounds method, not a new universal predicate or rights approval.
+
+## Historical source meaning and remaining limits
+
+The retained original administrative metadata describes the following source vintages and rights claims. These are the historical records carried through the inputs, not fresh grants or a present-day legal-boundary determination:

Counts and modern country labels do not establish administrative meaning. Bolivia's derivation and Colombia's unspecified canonical role remain explicit. No geometry substitution, coordinate transformation, provider-policy change, or licensing reapproval was performed.
+
+Panama's positive original scope remains rights-blocked under issue 2437; the numerical success of the five calls and retention of Panama as a foreign negative operand do not resolve that conflict or authorize publication of Panama geometry. The six-scope accounting remains 89,588 originals = 63,035 qualified + 3,884 territorial held + 22,669 Panama blocked. Honduras future preparation remains outside that accounting.
+
+The actual constructors explicitly limit their result to the requested native centres and retain original whole-source physical/hierarchy and historical source/resource limits. They delegate current owner-zero enforcement to native consumers. This review therefore supports the stated qualified products and preserved holds, while leaving acceptance, current ownership checks, integration and Panama rights resolution unclaimed. No shared branch, source data, geometry, or execution product was changed.

+"""Metadata preparation from whole retained originals; no spatial predicates.
+
+Reads exact accepted Git objects without lazy fetching. Outputs preserve complete
+consumed source and selected owner features for later stock physical execution.
+"""
+import collections
+import gzip
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import pathlib
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+REPO = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve(strict=True)
+OUT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).absolute()
+BASE = '21984e9ec4ec7370bc807e2da23cea2228747698'
+INPUT = sys.argv[3]
+assert len(INPUT) == 40
+PREFIX = 'coordination/engineering/egypt-original-repair-20261017/'
+QUEUE = 'coordination/engineering/global-current-cell-work-queue-20261014/'
+ENV = dict(os.environ, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH='1', GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS='1', GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS='0')
+assert not OUT.exists() and OUT.parent.is_dir()
+assert all(not p.is_symlink() for root in (REPO, OUT) for p in (root, *root.parents))
+inputs = {}
+def sha(body):
+    return hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
+def git(*args):
+    return subprocess.check_output(['git', '-c', 'protocol.allow=never', '-C', str(REPO), *args], env=ENV)
+def read(name, commit=BASE):
+    row = git('ls-tree', '-z', commit, '--', name).rstrip(b'\0')
+    metadata, member = row.split(b'\t')
+    mode, kind, oid = metadata.decode().split()
+    assert mode == '100644' and kind == 'blob' and member.decode() == name
+    body = git('cat-file', 'blob', oid)
+    assert hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(body)).encode() + b'\0' + body).hexdigest() == oid
+    pin = dict(commit=commit, path=name, mode=mode, git_blob_oid=oid, bytes=len(body), sha256=sha(body))
+    if name.endswith('.gz'):
+        body = gzip.decompress(body)
+        pin.update(decoded_bytes=len(body), decoded_sha256=sha(body))
+    inputs[commit, name] = pin
+    return body
+def js(name, commit=BASE):
+    return json.loads(read(name, commit))
+def encode(value):
+    return (json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n').encode()
+
+assert read(PREFIX + 'method/prepare-source-members.py', INPUT) == pathlib.Path(__file__).read_bytes()
+scope = js(PREFIX + 'original-claim-scope.json', INPUT)
+owners = {r['index']: r for r in scope['owners']}
+assert len(owners) == 167 and len(set(scope['complete_source_atoms'])) == 231
+roster = js(QUEUE + 'source-feature-roster.json.gz')
+by_source = {r['source_id']: r for r in roster}
+assert len(by_source) == len(roster) == 73567
+semantic = js('data/semantic-report.json')
+changes = collections.defaultdict(list)
+for row in semantic['changes']:
+    changes[row['id']].append(row)
+selected = {}
+whole_country = []
+for name in ('data/geography/part-7.json', 'data/geography/part-8.json', 'data/geography/part-28.json', 'data/geography/part-29.json'):
+    product = js(name)
+    assert product['type'] == 'FeatureCollection'
+    for feature in product['features']:
+        if feature['properties']['reference_owner'] == 'Egypt':
+            whole_country.append(feature)
+        if feature['id'] in {r['id'] for r in owners.values()}:
+            assert feature['id'] not in selected
+            selected[feature['id']] = feature
+assert len(selected) == len(owners)
+
+catalogue = js('coordination/engineering/original-geography-source-corpus-20261006/catalogue.json')
+metadata = js('data/administrative-sources.json')
+products, product_inventory = {}, []
+for family in ('gb:EGY:ADM1', 'gb:EGY:ADM2', 'gb:ISR:ADM1', 'gb:SAU:ADM1'):
+    record, = [r for r in catalogue['products'] if r['key'] == family]
+    chunks, offset = [], 0
+    for ordinal, part in enumerate(record['parts']):
+        assert part['ordinal'] == ordinal and part['offset'] == offset
+        decoded = read(part['path'])
+        pin = inputs[BASE, part['path']]
+        assert pin['bytes'] == part['bytes'] and pin['sha256'] == part['sha256']
+        assert len(decoded) == part['uncompressed_bytes'] and sha(decoded) == part['uncompressed_sha256']
+        chunks.append(decoded)
+        offset += len(decoded)
+    body = b''.join(chunks)
+    assert len(body) == record['original_bytes'] and sha(body) == record['original_sha256']
+    product = json.loads(body)
+    assert product['type'] == 'FeatureCollection'
+    assert product['crs']['properties']['name'] == 'urn:ogc:def:crs:OGC:1.3:CRS84'
+    originals = {family + ':' + f['properties']['shapeID']: f for f in product['features']}
+    assert len(originals) == len(product['features']) == record['feature_count'] == record['advertised_feature_count']
+    assert set(originals) == {r['source_id'] for r in roster if r['source_id'].startswith(family + ':')}
+    assert metadata[family]['sha256'] == record['original_sha256']
+    products[family] = originals
+    product_inventory.append(dict(source_family=family, original_bytes=len(body), original_sha256=sha(body),
+                                  features=len(originals), crs=product['crs'], metadata=metadata[family]))
+
+stages, membership, owner_associations = [], [], []
+for index, owner in sorted(owners.items()):
+    feature = selected[owner['id']]
+    properties = feature['properties']
+    assert feature['id'] == properties['id'] == owner['id']
+    assert properties['reference_owner'] == 'Egypt' and properties['parent_id'] == owner['province_id']
+    atoms = owner['source_atoms']
+    assert len(atoms) == len(set(atoms))
+    if atoms == [owner['id']]:
+        assert owner['id'] in products['gb:EGY:ADM2']
+        assert not properties['metadata'].get('source_member_ids')
+        association = 'direct-original-marakiz-or-aqsam'
+    else:
+        members = properties['metadata']['source_member_ids']
+        change, = changes[owner['id']]
+        assert sorted(members) == sorted(change['replaces']) == sorted(atoms)
+        assert properties['metadata']['location_basis'] == change['basis']
+        assert properties['metadata']['source_url'] == change['source']
+        association = 'accepted-complete-aggregation'
+    for atom in atoms:
+        row = by_source[atom]
+        assert row['family_index'] == 99 and row['owners'] == [index]
+        original = products['gb:EGY:ADM2'][atom]
+        stages.append(dict(target=atom, consumed=original, selected=feature))
+        membership.append(dict(source_id=atom, target_id=owner['id'], pixelIndex=index,
+                               source_ordinal=row['ordinal'], source_index=row['source_index']))
+    owner_associations.append(dict(id=owner['id'], pixelIndex=index, name=properties['name'],
+                                   association=association, source_atoms=atoms,
+                                   location_basis=properties['metadata'].get('location_basis'),
+                                   source_url=properties['metadata'].get('source_url')))
+assert len(stages) == len({s['target'] for s in stages}) == 231
+assert set(s['target'] for s in stages) == set(scope['complete_source_atoms'])
+stage_bytes = encode(stages)
+assessment = dict(version=1, kind='egypt-original-source-owner-preparation', accepted_commit=BASE,
+                  whole_physical_stage_targets=len(stages), whole_intended_owners=len(owners),
+                  complete_selected_country_owners_in_four_parts=len(whole_country),
+                  whole_stage_serialized_bytes=len(stage_bytes),
+                  whole_products=product_inventory, owner_associations=owner_associations,
+                  inputs=list(inputs.values()),
+                  limits=['Metadata association is not independent semantic approval, physical support, native qualification or owner-zero proof.',
+                          'Every original source atom and complete selected owner geometry is preserved. No polygon union, clipping, snapping or spatial predicate ran.',
+                          'Complete foreign applicability, geometric validity and whole physical execution remain pending.'])
+OUT.mkdir()
+outputs = {'source-target-membership.json': membership, 'source-owner-assessment.json': assessment}
+(OUT / 'original-stage-inputs.json').write_bytes(stage_bytes)
+for name, value in outputs.items():
+    (OUT / name).write_bytes(encode(value))
+print(json.dumps({k: assessment[k] for k in ['whole_physical_stage_targets', 'whole_intended_owners',
+                'complete_selected_country_owners_in_four_parts', 'whole_stage_serialized_bytes',
+                'accepted_commit']}))
